name: Radar
tech: Radar systems detect and track objects by transmitting radio waves and analyzing the signals that return. It interprets these return signals and displays the results. Because radar relies on reflected signals, it can miss objects or show objects that aren't really there.
dimensionNote: Awareness is the information available to you and how you interpret it.

name: Focus
tech: Focus directs system resources toward a selected task. Increasing attention in one area leaves fewer resources available for others.
dimensionNote: Focus is the direction of your attention. It concerns what occupies your awareness, what remains in the background, and how your attention is distributed.

name: Model
tech: A model is a simplified representation of a system. Models help explain, predict, and understand behavior by emphasizing some details while omitting others.
dimensionNote: Belief is the mental model you use to understand a situation. It includes your assumptions, expectations, interpretations, and understanding of how things work.

name: Run
tech: Program execution is the process of carrying out instructions and observing the resulting behavior. Some aspects of a program can only be understood while it is running.
dimensionNote: Action is the process of turning intention into behavior. It includes what you do, what you avoid doing, and what becomes possible through action.

name: Constraint
tech: Constraints are limits placed on a system. They define the conditions within which the system operates.
dimensionNote: Constraint is concerned with the limits affecting a situation. These limits may come from available resources, physical reality, responsibilities, rules, or circumstances.

name: Update
tech: An update modifies an existing system. Changes may alter how the system behaves while leaving much of it unchanged.
dimensionNote: Change is the process by which a situation becomes different over time. It includes what has changed, what remains the same, and how those changes affect the system.

name: Connection
tech: A connection allows two systems to exchange information or resources. A connection establishes the possibility of interaction, but does not guarantee that anything will be exchanged.
dimensionNote: Connection is the presence or absence of a link between people, ideas, systems, or parts of yourself.

name: Signal
tech: A signal carries information from one system to another. The quality of the signal affects how accurately that information is received.
dimensionNote: Communication is the exchange of information. It concerns what is expressed, what is received, and how meaning is conveyed.

name: Trust
tech: Trust determines which systems are accepted as reliable. Trusted systems are permitted to perform actions that untrusted systems cannot.
dimensionNote: Trust concerns confidence in people, systems, or yourself. It influences what you rely on, what you question, and where you accept uncertainty.

name: Sync
tech: Synchronization coordinates multiple systems so they operate together. Systems may remain different while sharing the same timing or state.
dimensionNote: Alignment concerns how well different parts of a situation work together. It includes timing, coordination, shared direction, and internal consistency.

name: Transaction
tech: A transaction exchanges resources between systems according to agreed rules. Once completed, both systems are left in a new state.
dimensionNote: Transaction concerns exchange. It includes what is given, what is received, and the terms under which that exchange takes place.

name: Firewall
tech: A firewall controls what is permitted to pass between systems. It filters traffic according to defined rules, allowing some connections while blocking others.
dimensionNote: Boundaries determine what you allow into your life and what you keep separate. They influence access, protection, and participation.
